title: The dark neutral medium is (mostly) molecular hydrogen
question: Determine the atomic or molecular character of the dark neutral medium (DNM) along 33 Galactic anticenter sightlines (and 46 total including Chamaeleon) and evaluate how HI saturation and the CO-H2 conversion factor influence DNM determinations.

data.sensitivity: rms optical depth integral error 0.003 to 1.138 km s^-1 over a 3 km s^-1 interval

what.value: N(DNM), 21cm HI column densities N(HI) and N(HI)_cl, and prior J=1-0 CO emission W_CO

evidence.quote: analyses of Planck Collaboration et al. (2015) and Remy et al. (2017, 2018) we take N(DNM) and Ł21 HI column densities N(HI) and N(HI) cl
3 Integrated J=1-0 CO emission used by Planck Collaboration et al. (2015) and Remy et al. (2017, 2018)

external_data.citation: Planck Collaboration et al. (2015); Remy et al. (2017, 2018)

what.value: 6 arcmin resolution dust-emission maps scaled to optical reddening E_B-V

evidence.quote: The 6 [′] resolution dust-emission maps scaled to optical reddening E B−V by Schlegel et al. (1998) are cited here.

what.value: Conversion between Planck 353 GHz dust optical depth and E_B-V

evidence.quote: Those reddening values can be converted to Planck 353 GHz dust optical depth using the relationship established by Planck Collaboration et al. (2014) between the 353 GHz dust optical depth and the E B−V values of Schlegel et al. (1998), E B−V /τ 353 = (1.49 ± 0.03) × 10 [4] mag.
In the outskirts of Chamaeleon, we used millimeter-wave HCO [+] absorption to show that the DNM was almost exclusively molecular, even while the gas as a whole was mostly atomic (Liszt et al. 2018).

Inferring N(H 2 ) from N(HCO [+] ) using the ratio N(HCO [+] )/N(H 2 ) = 3×10 [−][9], we combined these results with those from our earlier study of 13 directions where HCO [+] absorption was detected in the outskirts of Chamaeleon.

recipe.goal: Extract ALMA 89.2 GHz continuum fluxes and HCO+ optical depth absorption profiles
recipe.method: Acquire ALMA 89.2 GHz absorption profiles toward 33 compact extragalactic continuum sources and integrate optical depth (or compute 3-sigma upper limits over a 3 km s^-1 interval)
key_parameters: Spectral resolution 0.205 km s^-1, channel spacing 0.102 km s^-1, 3 km s^-1 interval for 3-sigma upper limits

recipe.goal: Measure J=1-0 CO emission with IRAM 30m
recipe.method: Average five-point frequency-switched CO J=1-0 maps (target plus four cardinal directions displaced by 2x22 arcsec) on the main beam antenna temperature scale and integrate emission
key_parameters: Offset 2 HPBW (2x22 arcsec); 3 km s^-1 interval for 3-sigma upper limits
assumptions: Contamination by CO absorption is negligible given the strength of emission and/or continuum

recipe.goal: Derive H2 column densities and CO-H2 conversion factors
recipe.method: Convert integrated HCO+ optical depth to N(HCO+) and then to N(H2), and compute molecular fraction f_H2, DNM fraction f_DNM, and X_CO = N(H2)/W_CO
assumptions: Standard Galactic X_CO = 2 x 10^20 cm^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1 for comparison

recipe.goal: Compare N(H2), N(DNM), N(HI), E_B-V, and W_CO across sightlines and regional hull
recipe.method: Combine the 33 anticenter sightlines with 13 Chamaeleon sightlines, bin quantities in 0.05 mag intervals of E_B-V, fit power-law N(H2)-E_B-V relation, and compute pixel-by-pixel cumulative distributions inside a regional hull
assumptions: Amount of material proportional to E_B-V and N(H2) = 10^21.0973 * E_B-V^1.335
